Learning it correctly means reaching the end of the stages of hearing and so forth and demonstrating it to others. "The thorough investigation of the entities of **Locanā** and the others" means meditating on them in the form of the four Mothers of the families. The "four women" are exactly four. "Day and night" means always. The phrase "with all ornaments" and so forth shows that they are adorned with innate qualities and the attributes of their attire. "The lotus of one's own heart" refers to one's own mind. The "lotus of the mouth" is the lotus of the face. "Expanded" means that after generating joy in that way, one should think: "whatever is the nature of the five chakras <note>energy centers</note> is mind-only, and nothing else." Through the phrase "the five rays of light" and so forth, it is shown that "one should experience that Great Bliss together with the stage of withdrawal <term>pratyāhāra</term>, characterized by the proximity of the senses and their objects." The phrase "acting in that way" and so forth shows that "one will become equal to the five Tathagatas such as **Vairocana**." "Acting together with even a single seal" refers to a yogi who possesses the practice without elaboration. —prevented. "Thoroughly learning the mantras and seals" refers to the <term>mantramudra</term> <gloss>symbolic seal of mantra</gloss> where the mantra is primary; this is the Great Vehicle of Secret Mantra. To "learn thoroughly" means to reach the end of the stages of hearing and so forth, and to show this to others. 

"The thorough investigation of the entities such as <term>Locana</term>" means meditating on them in the forms of the four Mothers of the Families. "Four women" means exactly four. "Day and night" means constantly. By the phrase "with all ornaments," and so forth, it is shown that they are adorned with "innate qualities" and the "qualities of their attire." 

"The lotus of one's own heart" refers to one's own mind. "The lotus of the mouth" is the lotus of the face. "Expanding" means generating joy in that way. After that, one should contemplate that whatever is the nature of the five chakras is "mind-only" and is not anything else. 

By the phrase "the five light rays," and so forth, it is shown that "one should experience Great Bliss together with that" through the stage of withdrawal, which is characterized by the engagement of the senses and their objects. By the phrase "acting in that way," it is shown that "one will become equal to the five <term>Tathagatas</term>," <term>Vairocana</term> and the others. 

The phrase "acting even with a single seal" refers to a practitioner who possesses the "unelaborate" <note>the path of simplicity or direct realization</note> conduct. The intention is: a practitioner of the Great Vajradhara and others takes a <term>mudra</term> <gloss>consort</gloss> from any class, such as a Brahmin. He generates himself and her into the forms of <term>Vairocana</term> and <term>Locana</term> and so forth. Traveling from place to place, eating whatever food is found, and entering into union in places secluded from people like forests, he trains in the "Clear Light," the nature of the complete purity of the three wisdoms. It is shown that "at that time, he becomes like the Great Vajradhara."
